text: Let ∼ be an equivalence relation on A. Which statement about equivalence classes [a] and [b] is always true?
explanation: This is the key lemma behind the partition theorem: any common element c gives a ∼ c and b ∼ c, hence a ∼ b and [a] = [b]. Distinct elements can share a class, so [a] = [b] does not force a = b.
